evidence: Cic. Phil. 4.4: cruentus sanguine cīvium Rōmānōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Covered or dripping with blood; in poetry also bloodthirsty (Mārs, Hor. C. 2.14.13), and of wars and days, bloody, cruel (Vell. 2.71.2).
The participle of cruentō, to stain with blood (manūs suōrum sanguine, Nep. Epam. 10.3).

phrases.latin: Genū tibi cruentum est; age, lavēmus.
phrases.english: Your knee’s all bloody; come on, let’s wash it.

sources: Lewis & Short: cruentus · Lewis & Short: cruento
